updateConnParams_signature_and_units:
VERIFIED verbatim from the 1.4.3 headers (local unzip of NimBLE_Arduino-1.4.3.zip, cross-checked vs raw.githubusercontent.com).

Declaration (src/NimBLEClient.h:70-71):
  void updateConnParams(uint16_t minInterval, uint16_t maxInterval,
                        uint16_t latency, uint16_t timeout);

Units (from the doxygen comment in src/NimBLEClient.cpp:470-473, quoted):
  - minInterval : "The minimum connection interval in 1.25ms units."
  - maxInterval : "The maximum connection interval in 1.25ms units."
  - latency     : "The number of packets allowed to skip (extends max interval)."  (slave latency = integer count of connection events that may be skipped)
  - timeout     : "The timeout time in 10ms units before disconnecting."  (supervision timeout)

Related pre-connect setter (src/NimBLEClient.h:67-69) uses the SAME units for the first four args:
  void setConnectionParams(uint16_t minInterval, uint16_t maxInterval,
                           uint16_t latency, uint16_t timeout,
                           uint16_t scanInterval=16, uint16_t scanWindow=16);
  (scanInterval/scanWindow are BLE-standard 0.625 ms units, but the 1.4.3 header does NOT state their units in a comment — flagged unverified below.)

RECOMMENDED VALUES for ~20 Hz notifications (50 ms target interval) on the ESP32 classic + scale:
  minInterval = 40   (40 * 1.25 ms = 50.0 ms)
  maxInterval = 48   (48 * 1.25 ms = 60.0 ms)  -- keeping min!=max gives the stack slack; use 40/40 if you want a hard ~50 ms
  latency     = 0    (slave latency 0 => a notification opportunity every connection event; raising latency raises effective worst-case latency)
  timeout     = 400  (400 * 10 ms = 4 s supervision timeout)
Call updateConnParams(...) only AFTER a connection is established (it calls ble_gap_update_params(m_conn_id,...)). The peripheral (scale) may reject/negotiate; it is not guaranteed to accept. Set the same values earlier with setConnectionParams(...) so the initial connection uses them too.
freertos_task_pattern:
NimBLE runs its OWN host task internally (created in NimBLEDevice::init, stack = CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_HOST_TASK_STACK_SIZE, default 4096 words, pinned to CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_PINNED_TO_CORE default 0). The notify callback fires in THAT host task context, not in your loop().

CRITICAL: src/NimBLEScan.cpp start(...) and NimBLEClient::connect(...) are BLOCKING — scan->start(5,false) blocks ~5 s; connect() blocks until connected or the connect timeout. They MUST NOT run in the 50 ms control loop or it will stall.

Recommended pattern:
  - Keep the 50 ms real-time control loop in Arduino loop() OR its own high-priority FreeRTOS task pinned to the OPPOSITE core from the NimBLE host task (e.g. control loop on core 1 if BLE host is on core 0). Use vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(50)) or, for tighter jitter, an esp_timer / MCPWM ISR; do not rely on loop() alone if drift matters.
  - Run all BLE work (scan, connect, reconnect) in a dedicated BLE task:
      xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(bleTask, "ble", 5120, NULL, 2, &bleTaskHandle, 0);
    Stack: minimum 4096 (match the host task) but 5120-6148 recommended for a central that builds std::string/vector scan results; 8192 to be safe. On classic ESP32 the NimBLE host task itself uses 4096 by default (raise via nimconfig CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_HOST_TASK_STACK_SIZE if you see stack overflows).
  - Do NOT call client->connect() from inside NimBLEClientCallbacks (onDisconnect/onConnect run in the host task). In onDisconnect, only set an atomic/flag (e.g. xEventGroupSetBits or std::atomic<bool> wantReconnect=true); the BLE task observes the flag and performs connect() itself.
  - Coordinate with an EventGroup/Semaphore, not polling sleeps, so the BLE task sleeps until the loop or a callback asks it to (re)connect.
thread_safety_answer:
volatile is NOT sufficient. The notify callback executes in the NimBLE host task (default core 0), while your control loop / loop() runs on core 1 — two different FreeRTOS tasks, possibly different cores. Sharing a float (weight) and a bool (e.g. connected / newData) needs real protection:
  - A single aligned 32-bit float store IS one ESP32 instruction (no tearing at the hardware level), but `volatile` gives NO cross-core memory visibility/ordering guarantee and does NOT make the write+flag a single atomic publication. The reader can observe the bool==true while seeing a stale/partial float, or the optimizer can reorder. So `volatile float g_weight; volatile bool g_ready;` is incorrect for a consistent pair.
  - Correct options (pick one):
    1) portMUX_TYPE spinlock: declare `portMUX_TYPE mux = portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED;` and wrap both the write (callback) and the read (loop) in `taskENTER_CRITICAL(&mux); ... taskEXIT_CRITICAL(&mux);`. This makes the float+flag update atomic and ordered across cores. Short critical sections only (the callback is in the BLE host task; never block inside it).
    2) std::atomic: `std::atomic<float> g_weight; std::atomic<bool> g_ready;` (C++11, available in ESP32 Arduino). atomic<float> is lock-based in the ESP32 libstdc++ but correct. Publish as: write g_weight, then g_ready.store(true, std::memory_order_release); read with acquire.
    3) FreeRTOS queue (cleanest for 'latest sample'): define `QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(1, sizeof(float));` and in the callback call `xQueueOverwriteFromISR(q, &w)` (safe from the host-task/ISR context) and in the loop `xQueueReceive(q, &w, 0)`. xQueueOverwrite keeps only the newest value; pair with a separate std::atomic<bool> g_connected for connection state. The queue also gives the memory-ordering guarantee for free.
  Rule of thumb: use a queue or portMUX for the weight value, and a std::atomic<bool> (or the same critical section) for any state flag. Never rely on `volatile` alone.
uuid16_vs_128_scanning:
VERIFIED. Relevant API (src/NimBLEAdvertisedDevice.h):
  NimBLEUUID getServiceUUID(uint8_t index = 0);
  uint8_t    getServiceUUIDCount();
  bool       isAdvertisingService(const NimBLEUUID &uuid);
Implementation (src/NimBLEAdvertisedDevice.cpp:503-512): isAdvertisingService() loops getServiceUUIDCount() and returns true on the first `uuid == getServiceUUID(i)`.

The comparison operator (src/NimBLEUUID.cpp:302-335, operator==) HANDLES the 16-bit<->128-bit mismatch: when the two UUIDs differ in type it builds the STANDARD Bluetooth base UUID 0000xxxx-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB and, for a 16-bit (or 32-bit) operand, memcpy's the short value into bytes 12-13/12-15 of that base, then memcmp's the 128-bit forms. So:
  - NimBLEUUID((uint16_t)0xFFB0) MATCHES an advertiser that broadcast the 128-bit expansion 0000FFB0-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB, AND vice-versa. isAdvertisingService() is therefore RELIABLE for the standard base UUID regardless of whether the device sent the 16-bit or 128-bit form in its AD payload.
  - Write the match as:  if (adv->isAdvertisingService(NimBLEUUID((uint16_t)0xFFB0))) { ... }   (NimBLEUUID("FFB0") is equivalent; both produce a BLE_UUID_TYPE_16 UUID). No manual 128-bit expansion string is needed.
CAVEATS:
  - Only works for the STANDARD base UUID. If the scale uses a CUSTOM 128-bit vendor base, the 16-bit form will NOT match and you must compare the full 128-bit NimBLEUUID("....").
  - The service UUID must actually appear in the advertisement's service-UUID list (AD types 0x02/0x03 = 16-bit, 0x06/0x07 = 128-bit). If the device puts the UUID only in the SCAN RESPONSE or as Service Data (0x16/0x21), getServiceUUID()/isAdvertisingService() won't see it — then match via getServiceDataUUID()/getServiceData() or via the device name / NimBLEAddress instead. Make sure your scan (scan->start) is configured to also capture scan responses (the default scan does).
reconnect_pattern_and_client_limit:
VERIFIED against src/NimBLEDevice.cpp.

Client pool / limit:
  - Default max simultaneous connections = CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS, default 3 (src/nimconfig.h:181-183). The ESP32 controller hard maximum is 9. This value is pushed to the controller as bt_cfg.ble_max_conn = CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS in NimBLEDevice::init (NimBLEDevice.cpp:875) — that is the real enforcement point.
  - createClient() (NimBLEDevice.cpp:216-226) does NOT reject at the limit: it only NIMBLE_LOGW("Number of clients exceeds Max connections...") and STILL `new NimBLEClient(...)` and pushes it onto m_cList. So spawning a fresh client on every disconnect grows m_cList without bound -> memory leak and the controller rejects new physical connections once ble_max_conn is hit.
  - deleteClient() (NimBLEDevice.cpp:235-272) is the correct teardown: it clears m_connEstablished, disconnects/cancels a pending connect, waits, removes the client from m_cList and delete s the object. Use it only at shutdown.
  - getClientListSize()/getClientList() let you audit the pool.
  - To RAISE the limit: #define CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS N in nimconfig.h (or -D build flag). For a single scale set it to 1 to free controller RAM (you still create exactly one client).

RECOMMENDED RECONNECT PATTERN (no leak):
  - Create the NimBLEClient ONCE (in setup() or the BLE task):  NimBLEClient* pClient = NimBLEDevice::createClient(scaleAddr);  pClient->setClientCallbacks(&cliCb);  pClient->setConnectTimeout(30);
  - The client object PERSISTS across disconnects (the stack does NOT auto-delete it; NimBLEClient.cpp calls onDisconnect but never deletes). Keep the pointer.
  - In NimBLEClientCallbacks::onDisconnect(NimBLEClient*) (signature verified: NO reason param in 1.4.3), do NOT deleteClient and do NOT call connect() directly. Just set an atomic flag / EventGroup bit (e.g. xEventGroupSetBits(eg, REQ_RECONNECT)).
  - The BLE task waits on that flag and calls pClient->connect(scaleAddr) again on the SAME object (optionally after pClient->discoverAttributes() if needed). Reusing the object means you never exceed the client pool and never leak.
  - Only call NimBLEDevice::deleteClient(pClient) when the app is terminating / you truly want to drop the slot.
  Avoid the anti-pattern: `createClient()` inside onDisconnect — that leaks clients until the controller saturates.
init_order_and_wifi_coexistence:
VERIFIED API: src/NimBLEDevice.h:98  static void init(const std::string &deviceName);

Order: NimBLEDevice::init() brings up the NimBLE host + ESP BT controller (esp_nimble_hci) and creates the host task. It has NO dependency on WiFi. There is no compile/link or runtime requirement that WiFi.begin() happen before or after init(). Practical guidance:
  - Call NimBLEDevice::init("scalesvc") once, before any BLE API (scan/createClient/connect). Put it after Serial/Arduino begin; its position relative to WiFi.begin() does not matter.
  - Both WiFi and BLE share the 2.4 GHz radio and are arbitrated by the ESP Wi-Fi/BT coexistence manager, which is ENABLED BY DEFAULT in ESP32 Arduino core 2.0.17. Do NOT disable esp_coex; let it manage time-sharing.

Pitfalls on classic ESP32 + core 2.0.17:
  1) HEAP PRESSURE: WiFi and BLE allocate from the same heap. With NIMBLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS>1, large ACL buffers, and big MTU, you can OOM — keep the nimconfig lean (see flash_size_reduction_options). Watch `ESP.getFreeHeap()` at runtime.
  2) RADIO CONTENTION: heavy WiFi throughput (e.g. continuous TCP/UDP) delays BLE scan/connect and can stretch connection intervals / cause missed events. Keep WiFi traffic bursty; for lowest BLE latency, momentarily throttle WiFi during the connect/subscribe phase, or accept latency=0 + modest interval so notifications are prioritized by the coex scheduler.
  3) CORE AFFINITY: NimBLE host task defaults to core 0 (CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_PINNED_TO_CORE, default 0). Pin your 50 ms control loop to core 1 so the two never contend on the same core. Do not pin the BLE task to the same core as the host task.
  4) The controller connection budget is set at init() from CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS — set it before init().

unverified_or_caveats:
1) NO BUILD WAS RUN. arduino-cli 1.5.1 + ESP32 core 2.0.17 are not installed on this macOS host; this reference is from direct inspection of the real 1.4.3 headers (unzipped from /Users/jamesalexander/Library/Arduino15/staging/libraries/NimBLE_Arduino-1.4.3.zip) cross-checked against raw.githubusercontent.com. All signatures are quoted verbatim and therefore compile-accurate for 1.4.3, but the <1.25 MB OTA budget was NOT measured — trim roles/buffers as shown and verify with `arduino-cli compile` + `esptool.py`/partitions size.
2) setConnectionParams() scanInterval/scanWindow units: BLE-standard 0.625 ms, but the 1.4.3 header comment for updateConnParams does NOT document scan param units (updateConnParams has no scan args). Treat scan units as unverified-from-comment.
3) SM_LEGACY/SM_SC are unconditionally #defined (nimconfig.h:225,228); no supported nimconfig toggle removes the security stack in 1.4.3.
4) updateConnParams() is a REQUEST; the peripheral (scale) may ignore or renegotiate. Not guaranteed to yield exactly 50 ms.
5) isAdvertisingService() only sees service-UUID AD types (0x02/0x03/0x06/0x07) of the STANDARD base UUID; custom 128-bit bases and service-DATA/scan-response-only UUIDs will not match a 16-bit query.
6) createClient() does not enforce the max-connection limit (only warns) — relying on it for leak prevention is wrong; the controller ble_max_conn is the real cap.
7) Default LOG_LEVEL is already 5 (NONE); if your build defines it lower (verbose), you lose ~64 kB — keep it 5.
